insights.concise_text: The comprehensive experiments on the IWSLT18 speech translation benchmark used lowercase BLEU as the evaluation metric for the reported 3.6 and 2.2 BLEU improvements.

triple.subject: comprehensive experiments on the IWSLT18 speech translation benchmark
triple.object: lowercase BLEU

insights.concise_text: The IWSLT18 speech translation benchmark experiments used ST-TED, whose tst2010, tst2013, tst2014, and tst2015 are test sets.
The 83-dimensional input features used by the CNN-BiLSTM architecture are 80-channel log-Mel filter bank and 3-dimensional pitch features extracted using Kaldi BIBREF14.

triple.subject: CNN-BiLSTM architecture
triple.object: 83-dimensional input features

insights.concise_text: The subword-level decoding and character-level decoding strategies correspond to the subword experiments with 5k tokens and character-level English and German sentences.

triple.subject: subword-level decoding and character-level decoding strategies
triple.object: 5k tokens and character-level English and German sentences

insights.concise_text: The vanilla ST baseline trained from scratch on the ST-TED corpus is one of the baselines implemented based on ESPnet BIBREF12 with RNN size $d=1024$.

triple.subject: vanilla ST baseline
triple.object: ESPnet BIBREF12 with RNN size $d=1024$

insights.concise_text: The end-to-end method that avoids error propagation in theory is experimentally compared with cascaded systems built by combining the ASR model and MT model used in pre-training baseline.

triple.subject: end-to-end method
triple.object: simple cascaded model over 2 BLEU scores

insights.concise_text: The ASR dataset, MT dataset, and ST dataset assumed available are instantiated by TED-LIUM2 corpus, ST-TED corpus and WIT3 plus WMT2018, and ST-TED.

triple.subject: ASR dataset, MT dataset, and ST dataset
triple.object: TED-LIUM2 corpus, ST-TED corpus and WIT3 plus WMT2018, and ST-TED

insights.concise_text: The scarcity of ST data motivates strategies to utilize ASR data and MT data, and the experiments provide TED-LIUM2 corpus as speech recognition data and WMT2018 as out-of-domain training data.

triple.subject: scarce ST data
triple.object: ASR data and MT data

insights.concise_text: The claim that char-level models outperform subword-level models in all settings is supported by the reported 2.2 BLEU improvement for character-level decoding versus 3.6 BLEU for subword-level decoding.

triple.subject: char-level models outperform subword-level models in all settings
triple.object: 3.6 and 2.2 BLEU scores

insights.concise_text: The lower-case BLEU evaluation is consistent with preprocessing that lowercases all sentences and removes punctuation to keep ST-TED and TED-LIUM2 transcripts consistent.

triple.subject: lowercase BLEU
triple.object: lowercase all the sentences and remove the punctuation

insights.concise_text: TCEN addresses the common practice's subnet waste, role mismatch, and non-pre-trained attention issues by reusing all subnets, keeping roles consistent, and pre-training the attention module.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: the common practice by solving subnet waste, role mismatch, and non-pre-trained attention issues

insights.concise_text: Because the common training practice suffers from subnet waste, role mismatch, and non-pre-trained attention issues, these issues severely limit end-to-end ST performance.

triple.subject: the common training practice
triple.object: end-to-end ST performance through subnet waste, role mismatch, and non-pre-trained attention issues

insights.concise_text: TCEN's tandem speech encoder and text encoder disentangle acoustic and linguistic feature extraction, addressing the role mismatch caused by the speech encoder's changing roles.

triple.subject: TCEN's tandem encoders
triple.object: role consistency by disentangling acoustic feature extraction and linguistic feature extraction

insights.concise_text: TCEN solves subnet waste by concatenating an ASR encoder and an MT encoder without an ASR decoder, unlike the common practice that discards the MT encoder.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: the common practice by reusing the MT encoder and removing the ASR decoder

insights.concise_text: TCEN reuses the pre-trained MT attention module in ST, addressing the prior limitation where task-specific attention modules left ST attention without pre-training benefit.

triple.subject: TCEN
triple.object: ST attention by reusing the pre-trained MT attention module

insights.concise_text: Because the text encoder consumes word embeddings in MT but speech encoder outputs in ST, TCEN shares the CTC projection matrix with the word embedding matrix to ensure semantic consistency.

triple.subject: semantic inconsistency between MT and ST inputs
triple.object: sharing the CTC projection matrix with the word embedding matrix

insights.concise_text: Because speech encoder outputs are much longer than word embeddings, TCEN lengthens MT source sentences with word repetitions and blank tokens to mimic CTC output sequences.

triple.subject: length inconsistency between speech encoder outputs and word embeddings
triple.object: lengthening MT source sentences with word repetitions and blank tokens

insights.concise_text: The ablation study supports TCEN's semantic and length consistency solutions, since removing MT noise or weight sharing degrades final translation quality.

triple.subject: the ablation study
triple.object: weight sharing and noisy MT input for final translation quality

insights.concise_text: The `-pretrain' ablation supports TCEN's pre-training and fine-tuning split, because removing pre-training and directly updating on three tasks dramatically decreases BLEU score.

triple.subject: the `-pretrain' experiment
triple.object: a dramatic decrease on BLEU score

insights.concise_text: TCEN's better start-point in fine-tuning supports the claim that its gain comes from bridging the pre-training and fine-tuning gap rather than a better fine-tuning process.

triple.subject: TCEN's better start-point in fine-tuning
triple.object: the gain from bridging the gap between pre-training and fine-tuning
